findings.note: BASELINE-001 was the only located programme in the operational-memory zone with no declaration, no engine and no gate: its register, its origin record, its certificate and its continuation classification were four markdown files. Consequently no gate could resolve which baseline was current, none could detect a missing, duplicated or out-of-order row, none could detect a break in succession, none could detect a baseline cited but never recorded, and none could detect that a recorded baseline had come to rest on evidence that no longer existed. Closed by DERIVING the chain from the located records rather than by authoring a second baseline register.
findings.title: The baseline chain was prose, so no gate could resolve a baseline

findings.note: The baseline register records the current certified baseline. The release lifecycle's header, its version history and the evolution governance model's header each still name the baseline that preceded it. Both sides are Repository Truth: the register records currency, and the release lifecycle owns the scheme and the version history. Deciding between them is reserved to the claim owner under CEP-002 Article 23.2; this measurement reads both, cites both, and refers. It does not edit either claimant — both are named in programme.forbidden_write_prefixes precisely so that it cannot.
findings.title: Located registers cite a baseline that the baseline register no longer records as current; the divergence is referred, not decided

findings.note: The located meta-constitutional projection carries a lineage-predecessor field on every registered artifact and declares an inheritance relationship type, and the located validator verifies that every recorded predecessor resolves. No artifact records a predecessor and no artifact declares an inheritance edge, so the invariant cannot currently fail and a vacuously satisfied invariant is indistinguishable from an enforced one. This measurement reports the population so the vacuity is visible. It does not populate the field: what an artifact inherits from is its own declaration to make under CMG-000001 XXXIX.6, and the field belongs to the meta-constitutional register, not to the baseline owner.
findings.title: The constitutional lineage invariant is satisfied vacuously, and the inheritance relationship type has no instances

findings.note: A baseline is a snapshot: the values it records were measured at the commit it names, and the register is append-only, so requiring a recorded value to still match a live re-measurement would require editing the record and would destroy the very immutability the baseline exists to provide. What this measurement therefore requires of a historical record is that its POINTERS still resolve — that the evidence a baseline was derived from is still present and re-readable — and not that its values still agree. A recorded fixed-point verdict measured against an earlier pipeline declaration remains a true statement about that declaration at that commit.
findings.title: A recorded baseline's measured values are historical; only its pointers are required to remain resolvable

findings.note: The located release lifecycle declares an ordinal baseline scheme and an operational convention of tagging a baseline with it. A version-control tag exists in that namespace formed from an abbreviated commit identity rather than an ordinal, and it is therefore not a citation of the ordinal family and not a recorded baseline. This measurement does not read version control: the containing commit and the tag namespace are owned by version control and are deliberately not restated in a record. The observation is disclosed here for the scheme owner. Nothing in this measurement depends on it.
findings.title: A tag exists in the baseline tag namespace under a convention the located scheme does not declare
